gaps.title: Approval and bank-detail verification steps not shown in the capture
gaps.description: The capture shows only the registrant's New supplier form. No screen, component or flow in the capture supports a Finance team member reviewing a submitted supplier, recording the phone verification of bank details, approving, or rejecting. These steps are not shown in the capture; it is unknown whether they exist in other mockups.
gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-002 and REQ-003 are must-haves and are the controls that stand between a new supplier and payment; DEC-001 and DEC-002 define who does them, but nothing in the mockup shows where or how.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The approver and verification workflow cannot be specified from the mockup; the separation-of-duties rule and the 'cannot approve until verified' rule have no observed place in the product.

gaps.title: How payment is blocked until a supplier is approved
gaps.description: REQ-002 says a supplier must be approved before it can be paid, but neither the requirements, the decisions nor the capture say where payments are made, how an unapproved supplier is prevented from being paid, or what payment-related state a supplier carries.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'What changes downstream after submission'

gaps.why_it_matters: Payment blocking is the purpose of the approval control; if the paying system is unaware of approval status, the control does not prevent payment to unverified bank accounts.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Suppliers could be paid before approval, defeating REQ-002 and exposing the business to payments to unverified accounts.

gaps.title: Bank details changed after approval
gaps.description: CQ-003 asked what happens if bank details are changed after approval; DEC-003 answered only the rejection path. Whether a change to an approved supplier's bank details requires re-verification and re-approval, who may make the change, and whether payments are held meanwhile is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Requests to change a supplier's bank details are a common route for payment-diversion fraud; REQ-003 verifies details only before the initial approval.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Verified details could be replaced after approval without the phone check, letting payments go to an unverified account.
research_questions: What controls do UK finance guidance and bodies such as UK Finance recommend for changes to supplier bank details to prevent mandate (payment-diversion) fraud?
Is Confirmation of Payee available for business-to-business payments in the UK, and how is it typically used when supplier bank details are added or changed?

gaps.title: Bank details captured as a file upload but defined as three data fields
gaps.description: DEC-004 defines bank details as account name, sort code and account number, and the VAT duplicate rule implies structured data. The captured form collects Bank details only through a file chooser, with no fields for account name, sort code or account number. Whether the file replaces, supplements or is unrelated to these fields is not resolved by any decision.
gaps.why_it_matters: The finance approver confirms bank details by phone (DEC-001) and payments depend on them; the form must capture the values that are verified and paid to.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The registration form and supplier record cannot be specified; the verified details and the stored details may differ.

gaps.title: Verification failure path versus rejection
gaps.description: DEC-001 says a supplier whose bank details do not match cannot be approved until corrected; DEC-003 says a rejected supplier returns to the registrant to correct and resubmit. It is not stated whether a failed phone verification is a rejection, who corrects the details, whether the supplier waits in a distinct state, or what happens if the supplier cannot be reached.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'Can a submission be edited, withdrawn or resubmitted after rejection?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The supplier lifecycle states and who acts in each depend on this; a correction made by the wrong person could bypass separation of duties from DEC-002.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Supplier states and transitions cannot be specified; corrected details might be approved without fresh verification.

gaps.title: Outcome of Submit for approval not shown in the capture
gaps.description: The Submit for approval button has no target, and only the default empty form was captured. Success, validation error (invalid VAT format, duplicate VAT number blocked per DEC-004), upload failure and loading states are not shown in the capture, nor is where the registrant goes after submitting or how they later find a returned supplier.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states
gaps.why_it_matters: DEC-004 introduces a blocking duplicate-VAT rule and DEC-003 a return-to-registrant path; both need visible outcomes for procurement staff.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Registrants may not know whether a supplier was submitted, why it was blocked, or that it was returned for correction.

gaps.title: Traceability of registration, verification and approval
gaps.description: No requirement or decision states what record is kept of who registered a supplier, who phoned the supplier, which independently sourced number was used, the verification outcome, and who approved or rejected and when.
gaps.why_it_matters: Enforcing that the approver differs from the registrant (DEC-002) and showing that the phone check used an independent source (DEC-001) both depend on recorded evidence; supplier approval releases payments.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Separation of duties cannot be checked and a disputed or fraudulent payment cannot be traced back to the verification performed.
research_questions: What audit evidence do common internal-control frameworks (for example COSO or UK audit practice for purchase-to-pay) expect for supplier master-data creation, bank detail verification and approval?

gaps.title: Who may register, view and edit suppliers and their bank details
gaps.description: Requirements name Procurement staff as registrants and the Finance team as approvers, but who may view stored bank details (or the uploaded file), edit a supplier, or see suppliers registered by others is not defined. How long bank details and rejected registrations are kept is also not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-002 'How are bank details protected and who can view them after upload?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Bank details are sensitive financial data and, for sole-trader suppliers, personal data; broad visibility or edit rights would also weaken the approval control.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Access to bank details cannot be specified, risking exposure of financial data and unauthorised edits.
research_questions: Under UK GDPR, are bank details of sole-trader or partnership suppliers personal data, and what retention and access-minimisation expectations apply?

gaps.title: Who is told when a supplier is submitted or returned
gaps.description: It is not defined how Finance team members learn a supplier awaits approval, or how the registrant learns their supplier was rejected and returned (DEC-003), through which channel, or what happens if a notice is not delivered.
gaps.why_it_matters: Any Finance team member can approve (DEC-002), so a submission with no prompt to the team may sit unnoticed and delay payment to the supplier.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Submitted or returned suppliers can stall without anyone knowing.

gaps.title: Non-UK suppliers and field formats
gaps.description: DEC-004 defines bank details as sort code and account number (UK domestic) and a format-only VAT check, but does not say which VAT number formats are accepted, whether non-UK suppliers can be registered, or which fields are required. No required markers are shown on the captured form.
gaps.why_it_matters: CQ-004 asked about non-UK suppliers and the answer did not address them; sort code and account number cannot hold overseas bank details.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Format validation may wrongly reject legitimate suppliers or accept malformed data; overseas suppliers may be unregistrable.
research_questions: What is the published format of UK VAT registration numbers (including GB and XI prefixes and group/government variants)?
What are the format and validity rules for UK sort codes and account numbers, including modulus checking as published by Pay.UK/Vocalink?

gaps.title: Duplicate and simultaneous submissions
gaps.description: DEC-004 blocks a supplier with the same VAT number as an existing one, but does not say whether pending or rejected suppliers count as existing, or what happens when two staff submit the same supplier at the same time or one person submits twice.
gaps.why_it_matters: Duplicate supplier records with the same bank details risk duplicate payments and split the approval history.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Duplicate suppliers may be created despite the VAT rule, or legitimate resubmissions may be blocked.

gaps.title: Accessibility of the registration form errors and file upload
gaps.description: How validation errors (VAT format, duplicate VAT) and submission status are announced, and how the file chooser is operated by keyboard and assistive technology, is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Procurement staff using assistive technology must be able to complete registration and understand why a supplier was blocked.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Error and status messages may be missed, leaving registrations failed without explanation.
research_questions: Which WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria apply to form error identification, status messages and file inputs, and what are the accepted techniques for each?

assumptions.text: The capture contains only the registrant's form; approver and verification screens may exist in parts of the mockup that were not captured.
assumptions.why: Inventory lists a single page and states other states were not captured.
assumptions.impact: GAP-001 and GAP-006 are treated as unobserved rather than absent.
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether further mockup screens exist for approval, verification, rejection and supplier lists.

assumptions.text: Membership of the Finance team and of Procurement staff can be determined from an existing role or group in the product.
assumptions.why: DEC-002 grants approval to any Finance team member, which requires the product to know who that is.
assumptions.impact: If no such role exists, the permission model in GAP-008 needs a defined source of team membership.
assumptions.to_confirm: How the product identifies Finance team and Procurement staff members.

proposed_status_changes.reason: DEC-004 defines bank details as account name, sort code and account number, but the captured form (SCR-002) collects bank details only as a file upload (GAP-004).
How payment is blocked before approval is not defined by any requirement or decision (GAP-002).
Handling of bank detail changes after approval was asked in CQ-003 but not answered by DEC-003 (GAP-003).
